transcript.text: hello there

transcript.speaker: agent
transcript.text: Hello — how is your eye doing since your surgery?

transcript.speaker: patient
transcript.text: It's fine, thanks.

transcript.speaker: agent
transcript.text: Glad to hear that. Are your eyes red?

transcript.speaker: patient
transcript.text: No, I don't have any eye redness.

transcript.speaker: agent
transcript.text: Okay. Are your eyes painful?

transcript.speaker: patient
transcript.text: No, I don't have any eye pain.

transcript.speaker: agent
transcript.text: Thanks. Has your vision improved as you expected since the surgery?

transcript.speaker: patient
transcript.text: I've noticed some mild blurry vision since the surgery, and I'm a bit concerned about it.

transcript.speaker: agent
transcript.text:
Thanks for letting me know. I’ve made a note to go into that. Would you mind if I first ask a few details about the blurriness, then come back to your concern?

Is the blurriness affecting distance, up close, or both?

transcript.speaker: patient
transcript.text: It's affecting both distance and up close vision.

transcript.speaker: agent
transcript.text: Thanks. Are you able to see clearly at a distance, such as watching TV?

transcript.speaker: patient
transcript.text: I have some mild blurriness when watching TV, so it's not completely clear.

transcript.speaker: agent
transcript.text: Okay. Are you able to see close up while reading?

transcript.speaker: patient
transcript.text: I experience mild blurriness when reading up close as well.

transcript.speaker: agent
transcript.text: Thanks. When exactly did you first notice the blurriness?

transcript.speaker: patient
transcript.text: I first noticed the mild blurriness shortly after the surgery.

transcript.speaker: agent
transcript.text: Thanks. Do you think the blurriness is getting better or worse over time?

transcript.speaker: patient
transcript.text: It seems to be staying about the same over time.

transcript.speaker: agent
transcript.text: Okay. Is the blurriness slightly hazy, or completely blurred?

transcript.speaker: patient
transcript.text: It's slightly hazy, not completely blurred.

transcript.speaker: agent
transcript.text: Thanks. Is the blurriness only when you are wearing your old glasses?

transcript.speaker: patient
transcript.text: The blurriness is there even without my old glasses.

transcript.speaker: agent
transcript.text: Thanks. Have you noticed any floaters since the surgery?

transcript.speaker: patient
transcript.text: No, I haven't noticed any floaters.

transcript.speaker: agent
transcript.text: Okay. Have you noticed any flashing lights since the surgery?

transcript.speaker: patient
transcript.text: No, I haven't noticed any flashing lights.

transcript.speaker: agent
transcript.text:
Thanks. You said the blurriness is mild, started shortly after surgery, affects both distance and reading, has stayed about the same, is slightly hazy, and is there even without your old glasses. You’ve also said there’s no redness, no pain, no floaters, and no flashing lights.

Is that summary correct?

transcript.speaker: patient
transcript.text: Yes, that's correct.

transcript.speaker: agent
transcript.text: Thanks — that’s all noted.

verdict.label: pass
